items.title: Common questions
items.text:
Is this therapy?

No. Alongside doesn't diagnose or treat anything, and it isn't a replacement for a doctor, therapist or emergency service. It gives your AI checked tools and points you to people who can help. See How safety works and Our promises.

Is it private?

Your conversation stays with your AI provider. Alongside only receives what your AI sends to its tools, and doesn't store it. There are no accounts. Read the full privacy policy.

Does it cost anything?

Alongside is free to use for now. Your AI app's own plan may affect whether you can add custom connectors.

items.title: Privacy policy
items.text: What Alongside can see, what it keeps, and your rights. Last updated: 10/07/2026

items.title: The short version
items.text:
• Your conversation stays put

    It stays with your AI provider. We never see the whole thing.

  • We store nothing

    We only receive what your AI sends to Alongside's tools, and we don't store it.

  • No accounts, no ads

    There are no accounts and no advertising, and we never sell data.

items.title: Who we are
items.text: Alongside is run by Alongside Health Ltd. For anything about privacy, contact privacy@alongside.london.

items.title: How Alongside works, and who sees what
items.text: Alongside is a tool that AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini connect to. Your conversation happens with your AI provider (for example Anthropic, OpenAI or Google), not with us, and your provider stores and processes it under its own privacy policy. Anything Alongside sends back to your AI becomes part of that conversation.

items.title: What Alongside receives
items.text: Only the information your AI sends when it uses one of our tools. Depending on the tool, this can be a country code, a topic name, or your answers to a wellbeing questionnaire. Questionnaire answers are about your health, so we treat them with particular care.

items.title: What we do with it
items.text:
We use it only to send back a response. We don't store tool inputs or results, we don't link them to you, and there are no user accounts.

Like any web service, our server writes a basic log line for each request, for security and reliability: the time, the address that was requested (for example /mcp) and whether it worked. It does not record what was sent to a tool, and it does not record your IP address, because the address it sees belongs to our hosting provider's network. Our hosting provider keeps these logs for up to 7 days.

The server is hosted by Fly.io in London (UK). Fly.io handles the network connection, so it can see the address that connects to our server. If you use Alongside through an AI service such as Claude, that connection is made from the AI provider's servers, so your own address is not shared with us or our host. If you connect from a command-line tool, it is made from your own device.

items.title: What we never do
items.text: We don't sell data, use it for advertising, or use it to train AI models.

items.title: This website
items.text: www.alongside.london is a static website. It doesn't use cookies or analytics. Its fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, so Google receives your IP address when a page loads. The site also remembers your light or dark display choice in your browser's local storage. As with any website, our hosting provider processes your IP address to deliver pages and protect against abuse.

items.title: Legal basis
items.text:
To the extent that we handle personal data, we rely on legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f) of the UK GDPR). Our interests are running and securing Alongside, answering the request your AI makes when it uses one of our tools, and delivering this website and protecting it against abuse. We keep what we handle to a minimum: there are no accounts, we don't store what your AI sends us, and our server logs record no content and no IP addresses. You can object to this at any time (see your rights below).

Nothing that reaches our server identifies you, and we store nothing, so we don't treat what your AI sends us, including questionnaire answers, as health information about an identifiable person. That is why we don't rely on a special-category condition. We still handle questionnaire answers with particular care.

items.title: Your rights
items.text: Under UK GDPR you can ask to access, correct or delete your personal data, and to object to or restrict how it's used. Because we don't keep tool data or accounts, there's usually nothing to retrieve, but please contact us with any request. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk.

items.title: Children
items.text: Alongside is only available through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, so the minimum age to use it is whatever your AI provider requires, and never under 13.

items.title: Changes
items.text: If anything changes, we'll update this page and the date at the top.

items.title: What we promise
items.text:
• Safety first

  • Never diagnoses

  • Cites its sources

    Content comes from the NHS, NIMH and published research, and the sources travel with it.

  • Not a replacement for care

    Alongside points you towards people who can help, rather than standing in for them.

items.title: Connect Alongside to your AI
items.text: Add Alongside in about a minute. You'll paste one web address into your AI app's settings, and your AI can then use Alongside's tools whenever they'd help.

items.title: Your address
items.text:
https://connect.alongside.london/mcp

This is the address you'll paste. Alongside doesn't need an account or password.

items.title: Choose your app
items.text:
• Claude

    claude.ai, the desktop app and mobile.

    Connect Claude

  • ChatGPT

    From the Plugins page, in a web browser.

    Connect ChatGPT

  • Claude Code and Gemini CLI

    For developers, from the command line.

    Connect a CLI

items.title: Check it's working
items.text:
Start a new chat (in ChatGPT, type @ and choose Alongside first) and ask: "What can Alongside help with?" It should mention crisis support, wellbeing check-ins, explainers, exercises and finding a professional.

If it doesn't, see Troubleshooting.

items.title: Connect Alongside to ChatGPT
items.text: Add Alongside as a custom MCP server from ChatGPT's Plugins page. Set it up in a web browser at chatgpt.com.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Go to Plugins at chatgpt.com/plugins.
  2. Select the plus button, then Add custom MCP server.
  3. Enter the name Alongside. A description is optional.

  4. Under Connection, paste the address:

    https://connect.alongside.london/mcp

  5. For Authentication, choose No authentication.

  6. ChatGPT shows a risk warning for every custom MCP server. Read it, then select I understand and want to continue.
  7. Select Create as a plugin.
  8. Find Alongside in your plugins and install it.
  9. In a new chat, type @ and choose Alongside, then send your message.

Note

Your account or workspace settings may restrict custom MCP servers. If you can't add one, ask your workspace admin.

items.title: Connect Alongside to Claude
items.text: On claude.ai, the desktop app and mobile.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Open Settings, then Connectors.
  2. Choose Add custom connector.

  3. Name it Alongside and paste the address:

    https://connect.alongside.london/mcp

  4. Save, then switch Alongside on from the tools menu in a chat.

Note

Custom connectors may depend on your Claude plan.

items.title: Need help right now?
items.text:
You don't have to be in immediate danger to reach out. These services are free, confidential and there to listen.

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call your emergency number now

  • United Kingdom: 999 or 112
  • Ireland: 112 or 999
  • United States: 911
  • Canada: 911
  • Australia: 000
  • New Zealand: 111
  • Brazil: 192

items.title: Crisis support
items.text: Alongside instructs your AI to share crisis lines first, before anything else, whenever someone mentions suicide, self-harm, harming others, abuse or feeling unsafe.

items.title: Which lines you get
items.text:
The lines depend on the country you're in. If your AI doesn't know where you are, it shares an international directory and asks.

For a country Alongside doesn't cover yet, your AI shares that directory and a reminder to contact local emergency services. It may also mention a national crisis line it knows of, but it will say plainly that Alongside hasn't checked that number, so please check it before relying on it.

Need help right now?

See the full list of crisis lines and emergency numbers on Help now.

items.title: Safety and how Alongside works
items.text: Alongside is a set of tools that AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can use during conversations about wellbeing. Your AI holds the conversation; Alongside gives it checked, sourced information to draw on instead of improvising.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
• What it does

    Shares crisis lines, offers two questionnaires, explains common experiences, guides exercises and points to care. See What it does.

  • What it never does

    Diagnoses, tells anyone they "have" a condition, provides treatment, or replaces a doctor, therapist or emergency service.

  • Safety first

    At any sign of risk, your AI is told to share crisis lines before anything else. See How safety works.

Not a medical device

Alongside does not provide diagnosis or treatment.

items.title: The limits of AI
items.text: AI assistants can make mistakes, and Alongside can't control everything your AI says. If something doesn't feel right, trust yourself and reach out to a person.

items.title: Report a concern
items.text: If you see Alongside give wrong or unsafe information, please tell us at safety@alongside.london. We read every report.

items.title: Safety comes first
items.text:
Alongside instructs the AI to share crisis lines first whenever someone mentions suicide, self-harm, harming others, abuse or feeling unsafe. See Crisis support and Help now.

On the PHQ-9, any answer above zero to the question about thoughts of death or self-harm triggers a safety check, whatever the total score.

items.title: What Alongside never does
items.text: It never diagnoses, and never tells anyone they "have" a condition. It doesn't provide treatment. It isn't an emergency service, and it isn't a replacement for a doctor or therapist.

items.title: About questionnaire results
items.text: A score is a prompt to talk to a GP or therapist, not a diagnosis. Only a clinician can say what it means for you. See Check-ins.

items.title: Where our content comes from
items.text:
• Explainers draw on the NHS and the US National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), and links to those sources are shared with the content. See Explainers.
  • PHQ-9: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams (2001), Journal of General Internal Medicine 16(9).
  • GAD-7: Spitzer et al. (2006), Archives of Internal Medicine 166(10).

About the questionnaires

The PHQ-9 and GAD-7 were developed by Drs Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them.

items.title: How we keep it accurate
items.text: Crisis lines are kept in one place and used for both this website and the tools your AI calls, so they can't drift apart. We check every crisis line and link regularly, and changes to safety content are reviewed before they go live.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
What Alongside never does

It never diagnoses, and never tells anyone they "have" a condition. It doesn't provide treatment. It isn't an emergency service, and it isn't a replacement for a doctor or therapist. See Safety.

items.title: Check-ins
items.text:
Alongside offers two widely used questionnaires, so you can put words to how you've been.

Questionnaire What it looks at Questions PHQ-9 Low mood (depressive symptoms) 9 GAD-7 Anxiety (anxiety symptoms) 7

Both ask how often you've been bothered by each problem over the last 2 weeks.

items.title: What a score means
items.text:
A score is a prompt to talk to a GP or therapist, not a diagnosis. Only a clinician can say what it means for you.

A safety check on the PHQ-9

Any answer above zero to the PHQ-9 question about thoughts of death or self-harm triggers a safety check, whatever the total score. See How safety works.
